# Current state (updated 2026-09-21)

> **Read this page first when taking over.** It answers "where are we now, what can be trusted, what hasn't been verified".
> The frozen contract is in [p0-spec](p0-spec.md), the acceptance criteria in `acceptance/`.

**The dataset grew, so the golden counts were deleted rather than re-sampled (2026-09-21).** The reference
dataset holds **1655** images / **220** subdirectories, not the 1653/219 recorded on 2026-09-17: the crop tool
archived two images and a subset directory was added. Every criterion that hardcoded those numbers went red -
**A2, A23**, `test_paths.py` (x2), `test_dataset_toml.py` - while **A1, the relative read-only guard, was
green in the same run**, which is what proves no *test* wrote them. Those criteria now assert that the plan
agrees with the **directory listing** (the per-subdirectory counts sum to the recursive count; one subset per
populated directory), which holds for any content. An exact count is a fact about *data*, not about *code*.

**The repository was prepared for publication and de-personalised on 2026-09-21** (MIT licence, CI,
community files; every local path and dataset/artist directory name removed). Paths now come from
`local_paths.ini` - gitignored, with a committed template whose defaults point at the sample dataset inside
this repository. Measured: the first simulation of a clean checkout (before the dataset criteria learned to
skip) had **21 failed + 21 errors**; the suite on a clone with **no private configuration at all** is green
(the gate line above). The Ubuntu CI jobs are reasoned, not measured: this machine has no Linux and no Docker.
See [changelog/open-source-readiness](changelog/open-source-readiness.md).

| **Batch write backup parity** (2026-09-19) | The batch rewrite backs the caption up before overwriting it (`backup`, default true), reusing the tagger's `backup_caption` primitive: byte-level, never overwrites an existing backup, no backup when nothing changes, and a backup that cannot be written **aborts the write**. Verified with real files through the shared `_batch_step` (5 criteria in `test_backup_overwrite.py`) plus **A40** (contract -> API -> files) and the panel harness carrying `backup:true`; falsified three ways (default off / call removed / checkbox off). |
| **Panel defect batch A** (2026-09-19) | The frontend defects that made "broken" look like "fine", none of which touches a contract: the tagger's diff never went stale on a scope change (it re-signed the preview's own paths, so a directory or selection change was invisible to it); an empty preview re-armed Run; an over-cap scope left Preview clickable; an accepted cancel looked exactly like a running job; a failed cache cancel could not be retried (no watchdog, unlike the other two panels); a failed model listing and a lost cache stream both looked like empty success; the scale summary read its checkbox at paint time instead of the request that was sent; and the scale panel's caption extension was editable only on the export tab. 10 new criteria across four test files, six new keys in all three packs. **The falsification caught one criterion that tested nothing** - breaking the preview cap left its test green, so it now pins the function body - and five other deliberate breaks each turned exactly the expected test red. The export's unguarded `dataset.toml` overwrite was deliberately left to the next batch (a contract change - it landed in the row below). One audit finding - "the preview's after column is wrong for four of the six write modes" - was **withdrawn and reverted** once the preview's semantics were questioned and checked against §4.5 ①: /preview reviews what the tagger produces, the write mode only decides how /run composes it, and folding the mode into the signature made a mode switch fake a stale preview and lock Run. |
| **Export `dataset.toml` safety** (2026-09-19) | The export used to `_atomic_write_text` a `dataset.toml` over whatever was at the destination - no existence check, no backup, no question - while the same job refuses to overwrite an image (`unique_destination`), and `dataset.toml` is exactly the kind of file a user hand-tunes. Now: an existing file is **left untouched** and reported as `dataset_toml_skipped` (with the reason in the warnings), and `overwrite_dataset_toml=true` copies the previous file to `dataset.toml.bak` before replacing it and reports `dataset_toml_backup`. The byte-level "never replace an existing backup" primitive was extracted from `backup_caption` into `core/captions.backup_file` and is now shared by both write paths. Criteria: 3 in `test_scale_api.py` (real endpoint, mtime included), 1 in `test_web_scale.py`, harness section 8 driving the real panel, and **A41** scoring skip -> replace -> replace-again. **Falsified five ways**: check disabled (3 red), backup call removed (3 red), the never-replace rule removed from `backup_file` (5 red, including two *caption* criteria - the shared primitive is covered from both sides), the panel default flipped, and the "left alone" branch deleted from the painter. No confirmation dialog was added: the operation stopped being destructive, so there is nothing to ask. |
| **Caption restore / undo** (2026-09-19) | The backup net had no way back: `.bak` files existed and nothing could put them back, so the batch panel still had to ask "are you sure?" before every write. Now `core/captions.restore_caption` writes the backup's bytes back (CRLF/BOM included), **invalidates the text-encoder cache in the same call** (invariant number one) and **consumes the backup** - keeping it would disarm rule 1 for every later write. `POST /captions/restore {images}` is the list form (per-entry results, `no_backup` as an entry, 403 for out of bounds, sharing the resolve helper with the batch write). The batch panel **no longer opens a dialog when the backup is on** - the toast carries 撤销 for exactly the images the job wrote, a cancelled run included - and asks again when the backup is off, which is what makes that checkbox load-bearing rather than decorative. `batch.cancelled` lost its now-false "cannot be undone" clause, and a toast carrying an action no longer retires on its own. Criteria: 5 in `test_backup_overwrite.py` §5, 2 in `test_web_batch.py`, harness sections 9-10 driving the real panel, and **A42**. **Falsified six ways**; the harness found a real bug (the undo list was read at click time, after the next run had cleared it), and two criteria turned out **insensitive** - the restored bytes equal the backup, so they now edit the caption in between before asserting the net was re-armed. |
| **Shared scope control** (2026-09-19) | Both panels that write captions have to answer "which images?" first, and they answered it differently: the tagger offered four scopes with live counts, the batch panel acted on whatever the filter tab happened to leave on screen and printed a bare count - a rule with no control on the panel that obeyed it. `web/js/scope.js` now owns the question (the four scopes, labels carrying live counts, the recursive scope showing "…" until its listing loads, the listing cached per directory, `onPaint`/`onChange` hooks for each panel's own reaction), and **both panels read the same `scopeProviders` from app.js** - the criterion is literally `app.count("...scopeProviders,") == 2`. The tagger is behaviour-identical (the code moved); the batch panel keeps its default (the filter result - silently changing what gets written would be worse) but that default is now visible and changeable on the panel that obeys it. Criteria: the contract criterion moved to scope.js with its original "asserting the literal appears is empty" lesson intact, static criteria in `test_web_batch.py`, and harness section 11 driving the real panel (the chosen scope reaches the request, the recursive count arrives, a scope change drops the preview and is reported to the app). **Falsified four ways**, each red in the layer that should catch it. **Superseded 2026-09-20**: each panel building its own control *was* the remaining defect - one control now serves the column and both panels subscribe to it, so the `app.count("...scopeProviders,") == 2` criterion is gone (replaced by a construction-site count across the frontend) - see [changelog/shared-scope-strip](changelog/shared-scope-strip.md). |
| **Job shelf** (2026-09-19) | Four panels start long jobs and each painted progress **inside its own tab**: switch tabs and a job that was still writing captions became invisible, and "which tab is busy" was not even a single answer (nothing serialises them). `web/js/jobs.js` is a shelf, not a second state machine: a panel registers the job it already owns and pushes the numbers it already paints (one source of truth per job), and the shelf renders one row per running job - workspace name (reusing the existing `tab.*` labels, so it added **no copy**), done/total + current file, and a cancel that calls that panel's own path. The row's label opens the owning tab. It sits outside every panel (the position *is* the feature) and every panel closes its row in its single job-end function, so done / a lost stream / a refused cancel / the watchdog all take it away. **It exposed a pre-existing hole**: the batch panel had `cancelling` but no cancel watchdog (the other three arm 30 s), which would have left a row forever - added, with `batch.cancelTimeout`. Criteria: `jobs_harness.mjs` (two jobs are two rows, cancel once, `active()` hands out copies), static criteria in `test_web_jobs.py` (host position, exactly three injections, the choke point per panel), and batch harness section 12 (row appears, follows progress, cancel reaches the endpoint, both endings remove it). **Falsified five ways**; the harness also caught a real defect in the shelf - a click on a button already replaced by a repaint - which hardened `cancel()` to be idempotent. |
| **Job resume across a reload** (2026-09-19) | A refresh used to wipe every running job while the backend kept writing. `web/js/jobstore.js` bookmarks the id in sessionStorage (per tab, one entry per panel, every operation tolerant of an absent/hostile/full storage), each panel remembers at start and forgets in its single job-end function, and `boot()` hands the bookmarks back through `resume(jobId, total, task)` - the streams replay their complete event logs, so no state has to be reconstructed and a job that ended during the reload replays its terminal event immediately. **This batch also uncovered that the tagger panel was unconstructible**: `autotag.js` called `createScopeControl` without importing it (from the previous commit), which parsed fine and left every gate green while the app could not start. Two criteria now close that hole: the locale harness **constructs the tagger panel** (removing the import again fails it with the exact ReferenceError), and `test_every_module_imports_the_helpers_it_calls` is a general net that found its own two flaws (multi-line imports, locally defined helpers sharing a name) while being written. |
| **Batch operation performance** (2026-09-19) | Baseline harness `tools/bench_batch_ops.py` (non-destructive: scratch only below a directory outside the repository, real dataset read-only). Measured on 16 cores: export 1536x1536 PNG (`optimize=True`) **1355 ms/image sequential -> 415 at 4 workers -> 272 at 8 (5.0x)** `optimize=False` 502; batch caption write 3.46 -> 0.85 ms/image; cache invalidate 0.30 ms/image; one caption per request 2.56 ms vs batched `POST /api/captions/read` 0.34 ms/image. At library scale: export **~36 min -> ~7.5 min**, batch write 5.7 s, cache rebuild 0.5 s, caption probe 691 requests -> 2. The parallel export's output is **byte-for-byte identical** to sequential (new criterion; **falsified**: dropping the reserved-name set makes two same-stem images claim one destination and the test turns red). Frontend: probe batches and refreshes once per chunk (the old per-image `applyFilter()` was O(N^2)). Details in [changelog/batch-performance](changelog/batch-performance.md) |

| **The strip's dataset.toml fact (§4.16, 2026-09-20)** | The third segment could only say `dataset.toml 未检查`, because no endpoint could tell the app whether the file exists (`POST /api/dataset/toml` is pure computation, and `dataset_toml_skipped` describes an export that already ran). `GET /api/dataset/toml/status?root=` now answers `{root, path, exists, mtime, size}` from **one `os.stat`**: read-only (the whole tree is fingerprinted before and after every call, and asking about a missing file does not create one), `exists` = a regular file (`S_ISREG`), and a failed stat is 500 `stat_failed` rather than "not there" (`Path.is_file()` would have swallowed it). **The subject is `state.root`, not `state.dir`** - the export panel is pointed at the directory on screen, so the old segment described another file at a subdirectory. The fact gates the claim: no answer = 未检查, a failed request = its own 检查失败 state, absent = 未生成 (a fact now, not the guess the previous round removed), present = 就绪 or the panel's own warning/skipped/inconsistent wording **only when that report is for the same root** - so a clean report with no file on disk reads 未生成 instead of 就绪. Re-asked on navigation, on the 15 s poll (whose fingerprint only sees images), after a finished export (`onFinished`: the one job here that writes a toml, into a target root that can be the dataset's own), and on a click (the retry). | **Scroll memory for directory navigation** (§4.15, 2026-09-19) | A user reported "going back up doesn't stop on the folder I just came from": every list is rebuilt wholesale on navigation (`replaceChildren`), so the scroll container snaps back to the top, and the left column has **219** rows. | **Test-loop tiers** (2026-09-20) | The test loop is two tiers now: `tools/check_relevant.py` runs only the tests and harnesses that name what changed (a frontend change costs ~1.5 s instead of ~80 s), reports anything no test names as UNCOVERED, and `--full` is the whole gate before reporting. 10 criteria in `test/test_check_relevant.py`, falsified five ways (two of them found *by* the falsification). Details in [changelog/test-loop-tiers](changelog/test-loop-tiers.md) |

| **The export acts on the scope strip's list** (§4.14, 2026-09-20) | The user reported that scaling exported the whole folder instead of the images they had picked, and the code agreed in writing: `api/scale.py` did `paths.iter_images(root, recursive=True)` and the panel carried a sentence admitting the scope did not apply. `POST /api/scale/run` now takes **`images`** - the column's scope strip, snapshotted when Start is pressed - and writes exactly those, in order; an empty or absent list is **400 `no_images`** rather than "then do the whole directory" (that fallback *is* the reported bug, so it is not kept), every entry is validated (allowlist → file → image extension → under `root`) with the first bad one rejecting the whole request, and a duplicate entry is one file. `root` keeps its job as the base the target tree mirrors. **The audit the same request asked for** found the crop panel reading the strip only in `onShow()` (**fixed**: it subscribes like the tagger and the batch panel, so picking images while its tab is open moves its gate) and two stale statements about which panels obey the strip (`scope.stripHint`, the `index.html` comment). Criteria: `test/test_scale_api.py` 27 → 36 (exactly the listed images, order, duplicates, the empty/absent list, the four rejection paths, and a recursive criterion whose list is built by `/api/fs/list` the way the strip builds its own), the scale harness over a **real `scope.js` control** (the request carries its list, an empty scope keeps Start disabled and says why, a change while the tab is open reaches the gate, a change between two runs reaches the second request), `test_web_scope.py`'s export criterion **inverted** (it had pinned the old deviation), the crop harness + `test_web_crop.py`, and A36 extended with the list's extent and the empty-list refusal. **Seven falsifications** (fallback for an empty list; ignoring the list; dedup removed; the under-`root` check removed; the builder returning `[]`; either panel's subscription removed), each red then green. **Not a real browser** (fake DOM, gap 5) and the request's own size at library scale is unmeasured - see the limits in [changelog/export-scope-list](changelog/export-scope-list.md) |

| **The recursive listing belongs to one directory** (2026-09-20) | Found by the previous row's review, one layer down: there the *panel* acted on a wider set than the control said; here the *control itself* described the wrong tree. `scope.js` cached the "directory + subdirectories" listing and trusted it whenever it was non-empty, **whatever directory it came from**, so after navigating it kept handing the previous directory's images to every panel acting on the scope - the batch caption write and the crop included - and a re-listing of the *same* directory (a crop archives beside its source) never invalidated it either, so the pre-crop tree stayed on screen until the user navigated away and back. Now the directory is part of the question (`cachedRecursive()` requires `recursive.dir === getDirKey()`; otherwise the count is `null` - "…", never a fabricated 0 - and `paths()` returns nothing), and `scope.invalidate()`, called by `openDir()` where the only fresh listings are installed, drops the cache and reloads it when that scope is selected. A plain repaint still costs no request, and nothing new polls. Criteria: section 6 of `scope_strip_harness.mjs` (real `scope.js` plus both panels: no fetch on a repaint; a dropped cache reads "…", then the new number, and the panels follow; another directory hands out **nothing** until its own listing arrives; navigating back reloads; the fetch counter asserted at every step) and `test_web_scope.py`'s static half. **Four falsifications**, one of which caught the criterion itself: with the two cases written in the wrong order, the cache-drop break left the harness green (the stale listing read as unknown for the other reason), so the order is now part of the criterion. See [changelog/scope-recursive-cache](changelog/scope-recursive-cache.md) |

| **The parameters remember themselves** (2026-09-21) | The report: "缩放参数需要持久化，不能每次打开网页都恢复成默认值". `trainparams.js` - the store the §4.9 export panel, the §4.14 scaling panel and the §4.17 crop panel already share - now reads one `kdt.trainParams` entry when it is built and writes it from a single `persist()` whenever a setter accepts a value, so the resolution / caption extension / resample / format / quality / optimize / no-upscale and the scaling panel's own `writeToml` are on the controls (and in the request body) on the next visit. The remembered field list is explicit and pinned by a criterion, because what is **not** in it is the point: the target directory (a location nobody chose in this session) and `overwrite_dataset_toml` (a permission for one run - the panel offers it per run, and the run that skips the file reports it). `RESAMPLE_NAMES` / `IMAGE_FORMATS` moved into the store (still pinned to the backend's tuples) so a remembered name this build no longer offers falls back to the default instead of reaching an empty `<select>` and a 422; a corrupt or foreign entry reads as "nothing stored", and a storage that throws on read or write does not break the store. **Four falsifications** (persist() a no-op; the permission remembered; the stored name unvalidated; the permission added to the snapshot), each red then green. See [changelog/remembered-panel-parameters](changelog/remembered-panel-parameters.md) |
## Unverified / known gaps

Sorted by "how far from usable", **the first is the most important**:

1. **Training has never actually been run once.** This is the only link not covered by any criterion, and it is the endpoint of the whole chain.
   The generated `dataset.toml` passed the trainer's own config validator (**static** acceptance),
   but "wire it up and it really trains" has never been verified. **This should be the next thing to do.**
2. **The cold-cache cost of export**: a full scan opens 1653 image headers, cold **14.65 s** / warm **0.33 s**.
   The endpoint is synchronous, so the first export click waits a dozen-odd seconds with no progress feedback. If this changes, make it a job+SSE (P1).
3. **Three warning codes have never fired on real data**: `[empty_dir]` / `[root_images]` / `[broken_image]`
   - none of that data's 219 directories is empty, and there are no broken images. Their bucketing is covered only by fake-response self-tests.
4. **The real ACL path for `[unreadable_dir]` is covered only by monkeypatch**: no directory was actually made
   unreadable with `icacls` (it needs admin, and it pollutes the test machine's permission state).
5. **Browser-level interaction - partly covered on 2026-09-18.** Using the local machine's Chrome MCP plugin (`ChromeMcpServer`,
   `127.0.0.1:12306`), these were verified in a **real browser + real data**: the zoom preview (image + side-by-side tags + edit),
   the directory picker, and the diff's red/green boxes, with 0 console exceptions. Details and tool limits are recorded in
   [changelog/ui-picker-and-zoom](changelog/ui-picker-and-zoom.md).
   **Still unverified**: tooltips on disabled buttons, focus traps in dialogs, layout across multiple monitors/scaling;
   and there is no repeatable automation like jsdom / Playwright (MCP is manual driving with a human in the loop).
   **The folder grid (§4.13) also hasn't been looked at in a browser**: the first-screen load of 219 cards, the lazy-load
   rhythm while scrolling, and how a 3×3 actually looks in a narrow sidebar rest only on a headless fixture and CSS rules.
   **The batch panel and the new filter controls (2026-09-18) likewise haven't**: `test/fixtures/batch_harness.mjs` /
   `filter_harness.mjs` are fake DOM (the batch one even fakes `fetch`); they can prove event wiring, request bodies and
   state machines, but not first-screen feel, the actual height of the common-tag row list in a narrow sidebar, or how the confirmation dialog reads.
   **Scroll memory for directory navigation (§4.15) likewise has only fixture evidence**: the fixture feeds **fake geometry**
   (`getBoundingClientRect` computed by the fixture from content offsets), which proves the centering algorithm and the wiring
   but not the actual landing point when centering across 219 rows, or whether the `is-revealed` highlight is visible enough in a dark theme.
   **Since 2026-09-20 there is a committed, repeatable layout probe** - `tools/measure_web_layout.py`,
   manual but real (`--width`/`--height`, canned `/api/*`, no backend, no dataset). It closes the
   *layout* half of this gap (the readiness strip, the scope strip, the dock and the three columns are
   re-measurable in one command, and it is where the last four rounds' tables should have come from),
   and it deliberately does **not** close the interaction half: no hovers, no keyboard, no dialogs, no
   first-screen feel. Those still rest on fixtures and reading.
6. **Linux still lacks GPU and macOS.** Borrowing a machine on the local network (Ubuntu 24.04) covered real-machine execution of the scripts,
   but **that machine has no GPU** (`nvidia-smi` doesn't exist), so the CUDA route and WD14 inference have no evidence on Linux;
   **macOS has never been run once** (the scripts avoid `mapfile` for compatibility with the bundled bash 3.2, but that isn't verified);
   interactively asking for the root directory, `--recreate` actually deleting, and auto-opening the browser are likewise unverified
   (on Windows too they have only static criteria). This machine still has **no WSL distro** (`wsl --status` gives no output, exit 50).
7. **The CUDA route**: verified to work (0.301 s/image, 14% faster than DirectML), but it adds 245 MB + a torch dependency
   + putting `torch/lib` on `PATH` (`os.add_dll_directory` **doesn't work**). It is not the default.
8. **Integration tests skip rather than fail on a machine without models**: `test_wd14_integration.py` uses `skipif`.
   On another machine A10 silently goes unverified.
9. **Preview is a synchronous request, capped at 32 images** (about 26 seconds). Tagging the whole library needs run (background job + SSE).
10. **Hand-editing `roots.txt` / `model_paths.txt` needs a restart to take effect.** This is **intentional** (§4.11: memory is authoritative at runtime),
    but it is a confusing behavior, so it is written down here; changing them in the UI takes effect immediately.
11. **The fallback path for a failed file write was only produced on tmp** (pointing `roots_file` at a nonexistent directory).
    A write has never actually been blocked with a read-only ACL.
12. **Image scaling/export (§4.14) is only verified at the fixture level.** The backend has TestClient and A36's real-file evidence, and the frontend has a
    headless fixture, but it has never been clicked in a real browser (the same class as gap 5), nor has a full export been run over the real 1653-image
    dataset - per-image decode/encode time is now measured (1355 ms/image sequential, 415 at 4 workers, 272 at 8, on 12 real images sampled from the largest real directory), but the library-wide total duration and the target directory's disk usage are still unmeasured. A library-wide export is a synchronous
    background job (with a progress stream) but has no resume: cancelling midway and exporting again **restarts from the first image**,
    and files already in the target directory become duplicate copies because of the dedup suffix, instead of being skipped.
    **2026-09-20**: the request carries the image list now (the scope strip's answer), so the panel's blast radius is the control's - but the list's own size at library scale (1655 paths, roughly 150 KB of JSON for "directory + subdirectories") is unmeasured, and there is still no resume. **Adjacent defect found by that round's review, fixed in its follow-up the same day**: the strip's "directory + subdirectories" entry was cached in `scope.js` without being tied to the directory it was loaded for (measured with a scratch probe: after the listing grew from 2 to 3 paths, `refresh()` still reported 2 with 1 fetch, and switching the scope away and back changed nothing), so the count - and, once the export took the scope's list, the export - described a tree that was not on screen: the one the user had just left, or the pre-crop one. The cache is now only an answer for the current directory and `scope.invalidate()` (called by `openDir()`) drops it whenever a fresh listing is installed - [changelog/scope-recursive-cache](changelog/scope-recursive-cache.md).
13. **Localization has been verified once in a real browser** (see [changelog/caption-dock](changelog/caption-dock.md) for what moved since: that run covered the then 7-tab strip under `?lang=en`),
    but the quality of the 448×3 translations **has not been reviewed one by one**, nor has the full "error → fix" flow been walked in an English/Japanese UI.
    The copy the backend produces still has gaps - export's `warnings`/`skipped`,
    `api/autotag.py`'s `errors[].message`, and the message in `{"error": {code, message}}`.
    Backend messages are written in English (this repository's working language), so under a zh-CN UI
    those sentences surface in English rather than Chinese. The structured `code + params` (frontend rendering `msg.*`) is in progress,
    and `web/js/strings.js` already has `hasKey()` ready for the "fall back to the original when there's no translation" degradation path.
14. **The China index profile (`setup_env_cn.*`) has never been run for real.** What was verified is the dry-run plan and the index-profile selection
    (both the Windows PowerShell and Git Bash paths were asserted); the "move to the next source only when the previous one fails" fallback
    exists only as a code path - no failure was staged to verify it, and it has never been run on a real Linux machine. Details in
    [changelog/pip-index-profiles](changelog/pip-index-profiles.md).

15. **The frontend UX and accessibility backlog (2026-09-19) - read from source, not reproduced in a browser.**
    Two read-only audits (Nielsen heuristics; keyboard and screen-reader pass) plus direct reading produced this list, ordered by user impact.
    Items marked *(verified)* were checked directly; the rest comes from the audit and still needs a live run.

    1. ~~A failed caption save does not block navigation~~ - **fixed 2026-09-19** ([changelog/caption-write-safety](changelog/caption-write-safety.md)): `flush()` reports `failed` and `activateImage` asks before leaving.
    2. ~~A sidebar tag edit never refreshes the caption cache~~ - **fixed 2026-09-19** ([changelog/caption-write-safety](changelog/caption-write-safety.md)): the sidebar save now calls `refreshCaption()` and `loadFrequency()`.
    3. ~~Batch write and "rebuild all caches" are single POSTs~~ - **fixed 2026-09-19** ([changelog/long-job-visibility](changelog/long-job-visibility.md), [changelog/batch-jobs](changelog/batch-jobs.md)): both are background jobs now - 202 `{job_id}`, an SSE stream with one progress per image, a cancel that stops between images, and panels that paint their progress and say how far a cancelled job got. The synchronous endpoints stay for the dry-run preview. *(audit)*
    4. ~~No in-flight state for directory scans, frequency loads, cache loads or toml generation~~ - **fixed 2026-09-19** ([changelog/failure-states](changelog/failure-states.md)): failures are no longer transient (sticky errors with Retry/Dismiss), the affected panel clears itself, a directory scan dims the panels it will replace and marks them `aria-busy`, and `dataset.toml` generation disables the button and swaps its label. *(audit)*
    5. ~~A failed load leaves the previous listing on screen~~ - **fixed 2026-09-19** ([changelog/failure-states](changelog/failure-states.md)): the cache list and the frequency table are cleared into an explicit failed state, with a retry. *(audit)*
    6. ~~Scale and export cancel can stick~~ - **fixed 2026-09-19** ([changelog/long-job-visibility](changelog/long-job-visibility.md)): a refused cancel unlocks the panel, an accepted one arms a 30 s watchdog, and a cancelled job keeps its real progress instead of painting 100%. *(audit)*
    7. ~~Dialogs neither trap nor restore focus~~ - **fixed 2026-09-19** ([changelog/keyboard-and-dialogs](changelog/keyboard-and-dialogs.md), [changelog/confirm-dialog-and-focus](changelog/confirm-dialog-and-focus.md)): the picker takes focus on open and ignores keys from outside itself; the picker, the zoom viewer and the model-roots dialog all hand focus back on close. Focus is not trapped, but every dialog now opens on a sensible control and returns the keyboard. *(audit; the missing `focus()` calls were verified)*
    8. ~~The frequency table is mouse-only~~ - **fixed 2026-09-19** ([changelog/keyboard-and-dialogs](changelog/keyboard-and-dialogs.md)): rows are real buttons, each carries its tri-state as an `sr-only` word, and a focus ring was added. *(verified)*
    9. ~~The tab strip is only visually tabs~~ - **fixed 2026-09-19** ([changelog/keyboard-and-dialogs](changelog/keyboard-and-dialogs.md)): `aria-selected`/`aria-controls`/`tabpanel`/roving tabindex/arrow keys/Home-End, plus a weight and underline change so the active tab is not colour-only. *(verified)*
    10. ~~Removing a root or a model directory asks nothing~~ - **fixed 2026-09-19** ([changelog/confirm-dialog-and-focus](changelog/confirm-dialog-and-focus.md)): both go through the in-app dialog now, which names the action and defaults to no. *(audit)*
    11. ~~Multiline captions: leaving raw mode silently truncates~~ - **fixed 2026-09-19** ([changelog/caption-write-safety](changelog/caption-write-safety.md)): `wouldDropLines()` gates the exit behind a confirmation, and the failure state now survives the repaint.
    12. ~~Smaller: chip names, alt text, `window.confirm`, dead copy~~ - **fixed 2026-09-19** ([changelog/keyboard-and-dialogs](changelog/keyboard-and-dialogs.md), [changelog/confirm-dialog-and-focus](changelog/confirm-dialog-and-focus.md)): chip remove buttons name their tag; tiles announce once (empty alt, caption carries the name), the enlargement announces the base name, diff rows carry a hidden file name; `window.confirm` is gone; and the last four unused copy keys were deleted. *(verified by grep)*

## One thing that was NOT done (don't assume it was)

[project-architecture](project-architecture.md) used to say "read `dataset.toml` and list the current job's dataset in the sidebar" -
**that was an early idea and was never implemented**. The actual relationship now is only: this tool **generates** `dataset.toml`,
and the trainer **reads** it. There are no inter-process calls between the two. (Found and fixed while tidying the docs on 2026-09-17.)

## Suggested next steps

1. **Run a real training pass on real data** (gap 1). This is the only thing that can prove the whole chain holds,
   and the entire reason this thing exists. Once it works, the defaults of the `dataset.toml` generator
   (especially `max_bucket_reso=4096`, which on this machine would scale 273/1653 images) should also be tuned against actual results.
2. Turn export, autotag preview, and batch-edit `dry_run` into background jobs (gaps 2, 9, and the "unverified" section of
   [changelog/tag-editing-and-filtering](changelog/tag-editing-and-filtering.md)) -
   the same pattern (job + SSE), so they can be done together.
3. To really use this on Linux: run the full tagger flow once on the machine **with a GPU** (or WSL + CUDA) (gap 6).
   Right now the Linux side only proves "the service starts, the API is right, the scripts are right", not "it can tag".
4. Add real broken-image samples and walk gaps 3 and 4's warning codes on real data.
5. **Missing-caption mode** - agreed 2026-09-20 and **shipped**: [changelog/missing-caption-mode](changelog/missing-caption-mode.md).
   Both decisions below are one invariant seen from both ends:
   **the selection is always a subset of what is on screen (`selected ⊆ visible = filter result`)**.
   - *Missing mode*: tag filtering and "select images missing a caption" (`#btn-select-missing`,
     `app.js` -> `gallery.selectMissing()`, `gallery.js`) govern **disjoint domains** - a tag filter
     talks about images that have captions, the button about the ones that do not - so today the button
     selects images the filter is hiding, and the batch write then hits images nobody can see.
     Fix: the button becomes a **mode switch** (leave tag filtering, show only caption-less images,
     select them all). Explicit mutual exclusion beats greying the button out.
   - *Pruning stays*: `setVisiblePaths` (`gallery.js`) deleting selected paths the filter hides is **the
     intended spec, not a defect** (the earlier proposal to make filtering purely visual was rejected).
     What follows from it: entering missing mode must clear tag filters, or the two disagree again.
   - Same root, separate defect: a caption-less image passes an **exclude-only** filter (`matchesFilter`,
     `filter.js`: an empty tag set satisfies `exclude`), so a "does not contain X" view lists images
     that have no tags at all. Pending/failed probes staying visible is deliberate (never hide a tile on
     a slow probe) and must be kept.
6. **Following a dataset that changes outside the app** - shipped 2026-09-20:
   [changelog/dataset-change-polling](changelog/dataset-change-polling.md). A 15 s poll of `/api/fs/list`
   (image count + newest mtime) re-lists on change, skipping while a job runs, in a background tab, or while
   a field has focus. **Still open**: the wait is up to 15 s, and a directory that is not open is not watched.
---
